references.observations: The current public visit uses the Denfert-Rochereau entrance and exits at 21 bis avenue René-Coty. The museum describes a 1.5 km route about 20 m below street level with 131 descending and 112 ascending steps.
The 2017 exit has a recessed white Corian surround, a projecting translucent canopy and original stone on either side.

Current entrance photographs show the three bays of the Ledoux pavilion, the hipped slate roof and the black-framed glazed entrance wing. Ossuary photographs show low limestone ceilings and stacked rows of bones.
The itinerary drawing provides a schematic relationship between the public entry, quarry galleries and ossuary, and distinguishes the Avenue René-Coty exit from the separate Fontis branch.

The public guide identifies the old quarry, Arcueil aqueduct, workshop and the crossroads between upper and lower quarry levels. It shows an arched entrance at the ramp and identifies the ossuary threshold, Samaritaine well and the barrel-shaped pillar in the Crypt of the Passion.

references.reference: Stop 9, Fontaine dite de la Samaritaine
references.observations: The museum photograph shows a low circular limestone curb below three curved guard rails, stepped sides and a raised rear sill. The positions and sizes of these details are estimated from the image.
The published stair photograph shows treads winding around a central stone support and a narrow handrail fixed to the outer shaft wall. It guides the modeled handrails and stair proportions.
The restoration photographs show plot 116 with stone plaques on the right, an upper band of forward-facing crania and a lower band of turned crania. The plaque bears the year 1792 in Roman numerals.

The city survey distinguishes surveyed quarry space from the visitor itinerary. It anchors the street context, while the modern visitor-room sequence and its gallery lengths still require separate evidence.
The photographed lintel has two lines of black text, above a deep stone reveal.
The flanking faces are painted charcoal with a long off-white diamond down each face.

references.credit: Gautier Deblonde / Les Catacombes de Paris
references.observations: A shallow stone bowl on a circular pedestal stands before two dark piers with pale painted panels.
The guide photo corroborates the piers and bowl.

The quarry workshop has a rough limestone ceiling, large supports and a low dry-stacked retaining wall. The 2024 museum report identifies both pillars cut from solid rock and pillars assembled from stacked quarry stones. The model approximates block dimensions and wall length within the existing draft route.

references.credit: Philippe Ladet / Paris Musées and Sara Boudjoghra / Musée Carnavalet - Catacombes
references.observations: The first three stops show a bevelled Avenue de Montsouris plaque, the 65 G. 1781 reinforcement mark cut into quarry stone, and the Arcueil aqueduct inscription spanning two lines between regards 24 and 25. The guide establishes their sequence. Wall sides, precise locations, stone sizes and letterforms are estimated.

quarryLevels.reference: Stop 5, Crossroads with the Lower Catacombs
quarryLevels.basis: Two levels and a connecting ramp are documented. The drop, gradient and shaft landing heights are model estimates. The museum's surface portals and approximate depth remain the external controls.

limitation: The modeled upper landings use independent PMTiles street portal frames. The revised gallery trace measures about 775 m. The Paris Musées planning diagram has an estimated 785 m public route when fitted to both portal shafts and the former Fontis address. Neither diagram trace nor the quarry atlas resolves the published 1.5 km visitor itinerary. The restored September Martyrs’ wall is represented at an estimated location.

shafts.result: The lower arches and upper platforms connect to the modeled spiral stairs. The detailed model retains the published 131 and 112 steps. The upper apertures fit within the mapped portal footprints.
shafts.upperConnections: The draft shaft centers move inside the mapped portal footprints. The upper landings meet the registered entrance and exit floor elevations. This fits the study to the street controls. The exact shafts and visitor rooms remain inferred.

reneCotyRoom.observation: The exit cutaway puts the spiral inside the room to the right of the street passage. The modeled landing ends toward the central passage through a side doorway. The footprint constrains the modeled rim, while its precise center and the room dimensions remain estimated.

ossuaryPlanCoverage.limitation: The visitor plan sets the relative position of the Lamp Crypt between the Samaritaine and later memorial galleries. The model uses a widened bend at the approximate stop. Its actual chamber footprint, measured dimensions and bearings are unresolved.

portMahonGuidedRoute.photoCredit: Gautier Deblonde / Les Catacombes de Paris
portMahonGuidedRoute.scope: The Port-Mahon branch uses the 2025 museum diagram and photographs. The relative layout, gallery height, tread count and well depth are reconstructed. The branch is a separately identified guided tour section. The exact underground alignment remains pending.

decureSculptureAlcoves.scope: The three Décure reliefs follow published photographs and the Port-Mahon branch shown on the 2025 museum plan. Alcove spacing, depth, side of the gallery and the exact relief dimensions remain estimated.

studies.title: Port Mahon
studies.observation: A front gatehouse, square crenellated towers and peaked rear turrets stand above the horseshoe basin, curved retaining walls and stepped forecourt.

studies.title: Port Philipe
studies.observation: The ramp climbs toward the tiered fortress and its round right tower. Below it a narrower flight falls away from a doorway. The label spells the name Port Philipe.

studies.title: Quartier de Cazerne
studies.observation: A colonnaded front with a raised center, end turrets and dormers stands above a sloping blind arcade.

fontis.title: Salle des Fontis
fontis.scope: The museum room plan documents 83 spiral steps from the Fontis vestibule toward the former exit at 36 rue Rémy-Dumoncel. The draft takes the 83-step spiral to the sampled ground elevation behind the photographed street frontage. The event gallery rises about 7 m across its 247 m modeled length, a visualization estimate consistent with an approximately 18 m depth at the Fontis end. The shaft center, grade profile and surface connection beyond the upper landing remain estimated.

addressControl.basis: The published plan names the outlet at 36 rue Rémy-Dumoncel. The mapped address constrains the end of the branch. The underground shaft position is unresolved.

lowerStairStudy.basis: The museum room plan documents 83 spiral steps from the Fontis vestibule toward the former exit at 36 rue Rémy-Dumoncel. The draft takes the 83-step spiral to the sampled ground elevation behind the photographed street frontage. The event gallery rises about 7 m across its 247 m modeled length, a visualization estimate consistent with an approximately 18 m depth at the Fontis end. The shaft center, grade profile and surface connection beyond the upper landing remain estimated.

frontage.observations: The historic photo shows a low ashlar frontage with a single narrow recessed doorway under a triangular stone hood. The tall wall behind it is distinct from the frontage. Only the low PMTiles footprint is a replacement in the draft. The draft keeps the street door closed.

pillarsHall.planRole: Upper quarry before the lower-level descent
pillarsHall.visible: A low case and wall display face an inclined reading plinth, with stone seat blocks beside the quarry wall.

ossuaryVestibule.planRole: Flat area after the quarry-level descent and before the painted ossuary gate
ossuaryVestibule.visible: Square piers built from large courses of pale ashlar, a large plaque on the left, and a clear aisle to the next passage.

renovatedInterior.limitation: The renovated Pillars Hall furnishings and ossuary vestibule stonework follow the museum’s April 2026 photos. The walking surface, stairs and room shapes follow the reconstructed plan. Their exact dimensions, underground locations and exhibit graphics remain estimated.

renovatedHague.observation: The visitor guide photograph shows a light segmented foundation, densely packed bone ends without evenly repeated bands and an irregular upper edge below the quarry roof.
renovatedHague.scope: The renovated hague follows stop 8 in the museum visitor guide, before the Samaritaine well. Its modeled wall side, length and position in the draft gallery are estimates.

passionCrypt.credit: Éric Emo / Musée Carnavalet – Catacombes / Roger-Viollet
passionCrypt.observation: The rounded pillar widens above the lower course and tapers at the ceiling. Three rows of rounded crania divide dense fields of long-bone ends. The first course sits directly on the floor.
passionCrypt.scope: The photograph establishes the casing profile and bands. Absolute dimensions, the chamber outline and its exact location remain estimates.

inscribedOssuaryPlaque.credit: Éric Emo / Musée Carnavalet - Catacombes / Roger-Viollet
inscribedOssuaryPlaque.observation: The pale tablet has two indented lobes along each side above a narrowing shaft. A row of small rounded crania runs beside its foot, with finer bone ends above.
inscribedOssuaryPlaque.scope: The museum’s stop 7 photograph establishes the plaque profile and bone arrangement. The visitor guide orders it after the ossuary gate and before the renovated hague. Its wall side, dimensions and position in the gallery are estimates.

tuileriesMemorial.credit: Éric Emo / Musée Carnavalet – Catacombes / Roger-Viollet
tuileriesMemorial.observations: A separate rectangular limestone stele stands on a broad plinth. Its curved crest meets two raised ends, with a narrow horizontal band below it. Five rows commemorate the fighting at the Château des Tuileries on 10 August 1792.
tuileriesMemorial.scope: The Tuileries memorial follows the museum photograph at stop 10. The draft places it after the September Martyrs wall and before the Crypt of the Passion. Its dimensions and wall position are estimated.

sacellum.observation: The Sacellum is a low side chamber. A pale trapezoidal altar widens above two rectangular steps. A wide square-topped tablet is flanked by two narrow arched tablets. Bone courses line the left return. The museum lists the chamber on its guided itinerary. The historic route description places it between the Samaritaine and the sepulchral lamp.
sacellum.limitations: The Sacellum uses the museum photograph for the stepped altar and the arrangement of the three tablets. Its chamber, wall side and distances are estimated between the Samaritaine and the lamp. Small lettering is unresolved.

septemberMartyrsMarker.observation: The marker stands at the right of the restored hague. The upper tablet has Greek, Latin and French lines and a Homer citation. The lower tablet has the Roman dedication, September abbreviation and year. A stepped plinth supports the two tablets.
septemberMartyrsMarker.scope: The close-up includes the Greek and Latin lines, dedication and year. The master adds the French translation, Homer citation and small date lines. The stylized strokes and marker dimensions are interpreted. The photograph does not locate the wall in geographic coordinates.

entryDepthInscription.scope: The April 2026 photograph shows the HAUTEUR depth inscription. Its position along the entry gallery and the dimensions of its stone panel are estimated. The historic number is reproduced on the sign. The current floor elevation follows the draft terrain and route controls.

easternOssuaryGallery.interpretation: The 2025 plan depicts the eastern and southern ossuary legs. The English guide routes the visitor toward the Crypt of the Passion via the eastern leg. The model represents the connection as an additional gallery. The 775 m through-route measurement uses the southern branch.
easternOssuaryGallery.limitation: The museum plan shows an additional east ossuary leg between the northern junction and the Crypt of the Passion approach. Its size, exact bearings and current direction of visitor travel remain estimated.

rueHallePlaque.credit: Eric Emo / Musée Carnavalet – Catacombes / Roger-Viollet
rueHallePlaque.captionEvidence: Two lines of shallow serif carving on a pale stone inset in the reinforcement wall.
rueHallePlaque.limitation: The museum photograph records the incised Rue Hallé plaque in a quarry reinforcement wall. The model places it in the lower approach near the PMTiles street crossing. The actual passage location, wall side and plaque dimensions remain estimated.

denfertLandingRoom.observation: The Denfert axonometric section shows a turn from the visitor corridor through a walled approach room to the head of the spiral.
denfertLandingRoom.model: The model adds plaster partition walls and a framed doorway inside the fitted annex at the upper landing datum.
denfertLandingRoom.limitations: The Denfert stair approach uses a short enclosed room and open doorway, based on the architect’s cutaway. The door, shaft and partition positions within the footprint remain approximate.

reneCotyGalleryReturn.comparisonAttachment: Annexe 6 · Plan des galeries, scénario parcours, option 2
reneCotyGalleryReturn.planningSourceType: Public preview of a Paris Musées route planning attachment
reneCotyGalleryReturn.geometryBasis: The Paris Musées planning diagram marks the bends toward René-Coty and a separate guided branch toward the former Fontis exit. The revised draft follows the exit-side return and joins the Fontis gallery there. Registration uses both public portals and the Fontis address. Exact junction geometry and final as-built underground positions remain estimates.

controlTiepoints.name: Fontis former exit at 36 rue Rémy-Dumoncel

reneCotyGalleryReturn.limitation: The draft public centerline measures 775.2 m. The Paris Musées planning trace measures about 785 m when fitted to the two public portals and former Fontis address. The museum lists a 1.5 km visit. The difference remains unresolved.
